extracted.intended_audience: attorneys seeking reinstatement to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office; counsel representing such applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of a petition for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO under the Office of Enrollment and Discipline procedures, including supporting affidavit(s) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and review by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a Petition for Reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for reinstatement must be filed and will be considered by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (example: the Petition for Reinstatement of David B. Newman received on December 31, 2015 was considered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision notes the petition was received and considered; timely filing and receipt by the Office is implied as a procedural prerequisite to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Affidavit under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition should be supported by an affidavit submitted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (the petitioner, through counsel, filed such an affidavit in support of the petition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision expressly references an affidavit under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as supporting material for the petition, indicating that compliance with that regulatory affidavit requirement is a substantive element of a reinstatement submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's Review and Determination of Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: After review of the petition and supporting affidavit, the Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline determines whether reinstatement to practice before the USPTO is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision reflects that the Director makes an evaluative judgment (here, the Director determined reinstatement was appropriate and granted the petition); this indicates ultimate authority rests with the Director to grant or deny reinstatement based on the petition and supporting evidence.
